The story effectively balances the compression of long periods with the slowing down of pivotal moments to track the evolving relationship between the narrator and her mother-in-law, Miss Emily. The narrative spans roughly eight months (from March to Thanksgiving) while also weaving in compressed backstory—such as the narrator's three-month courtship with Calvin and her eleven years at Kroger—in just a few brief paragraphs. Similarly, months of the narrator's first year of marriage and her weekly Tuesday phone calls with Miss Emily are condensed into a quick montage of critiques and classes. This compression allows the writer to slow down and give full weight to specific, crucial scenes—like the first dinner in March, the September fundraiser, and the November grocery store trip—where the characters' class dynamics and hidden connections are revealed in real time.
